conviction_note: Nothing company-level and unpriced was found; the Q2 base ($0.64 adjusted incl. ~$0.006 of non-recurring event interest income) plus one extra day and a smaller share count puts core run-rate at or a cent above the $0.63 bar, the sector is down ~10% into the print while HOMB credit was improving, and 5 of 7 prior prints rose, so p_up 55 on a 3.0% scale; impact_sum +0.6 and impact_scaled +0.3 agree in sign and are both small because no finding is decisive.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS consensus $0.63 (Benzinga https://www.benzinga.com/quote/HOMB/earnings-forecasts and Earnings Whispers https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/HOMB agree; Tickflow 5-analyst avg $0.62, range $0.61-0.63); revenue ~$293-294m (EW $293m, Benzinga ~$293.9m). No company guidance is given (Q2 release has no numeric outlook). Two agreeing sources, so sizes are not capped for the bar.
positioning_check: Short interest 9,907,152 sh at 2026-09-30 settlement, ~5.0% of 200.05m shares outstanding, 5.98 days to cover (Equibles/FINRA, https://equibles.com/stocks/homb/short-interest, read 2026-10-14 by the sweep). Not crowded. No usable option chain (baseline options.status empty_chain), so no skew; Unusual Whales quotes an expected move of +/-6.15% (https://unusualwhales.com/stock/HOMB/earnings), unverified and well above the 2.14% median historical reaction. Realised vol 20d 13.8%. Run-up -5.65% over 20d, -10.9% from 52w high, against KRE -9.7% from 75.27 (2026-09-04) to 67.99 intraday 2026-10-14 (Yahoo chart), so the drawdown is sector beta, not stock-specific.

findings.finding: Q2 2026 adjusted EPS was $0.64 on NIM 4.51%, of which 4bp ($1.7m) was non-recurring event interest income and 6bp purchase accounting accretion ($3.6m); stripping the event income leaves core ~$0.635, and Q3 adds one day of NII (92 vs 91 days, ~+$2.6m pre-tax, ~+$0.01) and a slightly smaller share count (200.46m at 6/30 to 200.05m at 8/6 after ~0.4m July buybacks), so a flat-margin run-rate lands at ~$0.64 against the $0.63 consensus — a one-cent beat lean, with provision ($5.2m in Q2, NCOs $5.8m) the main swing factor.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 adjusted beat ($0.64 vs ~$0.61-0.62) with record revenue: +4.78%. Q1 2026: -3.36% (Stephens cited weaker loan yields). Q3 2025: -3.39% on the Zions/WAL sector selloff day. 5 of 7 prints up, median |move| 2.14%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus of $0.63 sits below the Q2 adjusted $0.64, i.e. the street has modelled a slight step-down (presumably the event income and loan-yield pressure); if the market expected the extra-day and buyback effects, consensus would read $0.64-0.65. The edge is one cent and is within provision noise.
findings.independence: Share count from the 10-Q cover, a different document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1331520/000133152026000112/homb-20260630.htm (200,049,630 shares as of 2026-08-06).

findings.finding: Organic loan growth stalled in Q2 2026: total loans +$1.49bn to $17.13bn but ~$1.47bn was acquired Mountain Commerce, leaving organic +$24m (+$46.4m community banking, -$22.6m Centennial CFG, now $2.04bn); with no organic growth, Q3 NII depends on margin and accretion, and a second flat quarter would weigh on the forward read the stock trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 print with weaker loan yields sold off -3.36%; Q2 call cited >$1.4bn of production and Florida optimism and the stock rose +4.78%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is in the Q2 release and the sweep lists it as wire knowledge. What is unpriced is only whether Q3 continues the stall; WFC average loans +1% QoQ is the only Q3 loan datapoint found and is a weak proxy for a Southeast community bank.
findings.independence: Q2 call summaries cite >$1.4bn of loan production and management optimism on Florida (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-15-home-bancshares-inc-conway-ar-stock/), which cuts the other way; WFC Q3 average loans +1% QoQ (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000072971/000007297126000318/wfc3qer10-13x26ex991xrelea.htm).

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, the first hike since 2023; for a bank running a 4.51% NIM with $19.1bn of deposits, the hike touches only ~2 weeks of Q3 but sets up the Q4 margin commentary on the call, positive if HOMB remains asset-sensitive (not verified in the 10-Q text read).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior HOMB print in the baseline window followed a hike; margin stability commentary accompanied the +4.78% Q2 reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro fact is fully public; what is not priced is HOMB's own read of it on the 2026-10-15 call. If the market priced a margin benefit, regional banks would not have fallen ~7% since the hike (KRE 74.05 on 9/15 to 67.99 on 10/14). Proxy, sized small.
findings.independence: WFC Q3 2026 NIM flat at 2.43% QoQ (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000072971/000007297126000318/wfc3qer10-13x26ex991xrelea.htm), a large-bank read that neither confirms nor contradicts; proxy only.

findings.finding: HOMB goes into the print with the sector drawdown already in the price (KRE -9.7% from 75.27 on 2026-09-04 to 67.99 intraday on 2026-10-14; HOMB -5.65% over 20 sessions) while its own Q2 credit was improving — NPLs 1.08% of loans from 1.16%, NPAs 0.93% from 0.97%, allowance 1.92% covering 177% of NPLs, and management saying the large non-performing credit should create no further loss; a clean credit print against a credit-fearful tape is the setup for relief.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 print landed in the Zions/WAL credit scare week and fell -3.39%; in calmer tapes 4 of 5 prints rose.
findings.why_not_priced: The sector selloff is priced into HOMB; what is not priced is whether HOMB's own credit stays clean. If the market believed HOMB were insulated, it would have held up rather than falling ~60% as much as KRE. Large-bank Q3 credit was only mildly worse (WFC NCO rate 0.38% from 0.34%), which does not support a sector-wide credit event.
findings.independence: Credit metrics from the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001331520/000133152026000106/homb063026earningsrelease.htm); WFC Q3 credit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000072971/000007297126000318/wfc3qer10-13x26ex991xrelea.htm). Different documents.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no skew and a modest median reaction of 2.14%; the small positive lean agrees with the 5-of-7 up history and cuts slightly against the -5.65% run-up, which is sector beta rather than a stock-specific priced disappointment.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the reported-quarter EPS lean cut from +0.4 to +0.3 because this name's beats have been sold as often as bought (Q1 2026 -3.36%, Q3 2025 -3.39%, Q2 2026 +4.78%).
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): bar confirmed by two agreeing sources ($0.63 Benzinga and Earnings Whispers), so no cap applied; left the rest standing.
